content.text: Balance is not the smooth flow of feeling or the absence of response. The objective is the quality of becoming unswayed. A perfectly balanced entity, confronted with aggression, still responds. The response is love.

Balance does not produce indifference or objectivity. It is a finely tuned {term:compassion} that sees all things as love. When an entity achieves this seeing, the {term:catalyst} of experience is no longer needed — the entity has learned what the catalyst was designed to teach and has become a co-Creator of its own experience.

The being is not a machine. It is something more like a tone poem — a living composition in which each {term:energy-centers} contributes its unique note. The goal is not rigid placement of each note but the fluid and balanced blending of all, so that {term:intelligent-energy} moves through with minimal {term:distortion}.

The progression toward balance follows a natural arc. It begins with peripheral concerns — patience and impatience, desire and aversion — and gradually moves toward deeper territory: the acceptance of the self as whole and perfect, then the acceptance of the self as the Creator.

This central work cannot be rushed. The distortions of the self must first be known before the self can be accepted. Each thought, reaction, and pattern of behavior must be examined at its foundation. Only then does acceptance become real rather than merely spoken.
The specific practice begins with a prerequisite: the ability to hold silence within the self at a steady state. The inner landscape must become still and receptive.

Step one: examination of the self. Where patience is found, the corresponding impatience is consciously located. Where love is found, the corresponding fear. Each thought has its antithesis. The disciplines of the mind involve identifying both what the self approves and disapproves within itself, then holding each quality together with its opposite.
This is not suppression. Both poles are amplified within the awareness. The mind contains all things. The seeker must discover this completeness within the self.

Step two: {term:acceptance}. Having seen both polarities, both are accepted as part of the completeness within the self. It is not for a being of polarity to pick and choose among attributes, building roles that create further blockages. Each acceptance smooths the distortions that the faculty of assessment engenders.

Step three: the same work extended to other selves. In each other entity there also exists completeness. When patience is viewed in another, the corresponding impatience must also be understood. When impatience is viewed, the full picture — impatience and patience together — must be held.
Step four: acceptance of these other-self polarities, mirroring step two.

In daily practice, this is applied at the close of each day. The entity reviews its experiences, examines charged responses, and locates them within the energy center map. Over time, situations that once carried emotional charge are met simply as opportunities for service.

Repression is not the path. If a response arises during the day — anger, jealousy, grief — it is far better to allow the experience to express itself fully. Only when the moment has passed does the balancing exercise begin.

The progression of the balancing work moves from periphery to center — from specific distortions to the most central task: the acceptance of the self as whole and perfect, and then the acceptance of the self as the Creator.

This central acceptance cannot be reached by skipping the earlier work. The foundation must be laid with care. Each thought and action must be scrutinized for the precise foundation of each reaction. Without this, the claim of self-acceptance is only a word, not a lived reality.

When the work is done, acceptance of the self leads inevitably to acceptance of the Creator. The two are not separate acts. To accept the self fully, including every distortion and shadow, is to accept the Creator who made the self and who is the self.

The deepest healing is the recognition that the self is already whole. The distortions and blockages are real within the illusion and deserve full attention and care. But beneath them lies a being that was never damaged. The work is clearing away what obscures this truth, not constructing something that was not there before.

The crystallized healer is a channel for intelligent energy which offers an opportunity to an entity that it might heal itself. In no case is there any other description of {term:healing}. The healer does not heal.

The responsibility for healing lies always with the one who is healed. The healer's role is to offer an opportunity for realignment — the chance to see the self in a new configuration, to accept a different arrangement of energies. Whether the entity accepts this is a matter of its own free will.
If the entity, at any level, desires to remain in its current pattern of distortion, it will do so. Even the most crystallized channel cannot impose healing upon one who does not choose it.

Healing energy moves from the heart center — from green ray. Healing through yellow ray (personal will or power) may transfer energy, but the one receiving may come to depend upon the healer rather than discovering its own capacity. Green-ray healing penetrates deeper, offering the entity the opportunity to reconfigure its own energy patterns from within.

When the one wishing to be healed, though sincere, remains unhealed, {term:pre-incarnative-choice} may be at work. Some conditions were chosen before birth as part of the entity's learning. The most helpful service may be to suggest meditation upon the affirmative uses of whatever limitations the entity experiences.

A crystallized entity — one whose {term:energy-centers} are balanced and unblocked — becomes analogous in function to structures of sacred geometry that concentrate and direct light. Energy enters through the being, spirals through the energy centers, and is channeled through green ray before being offered to the one who seeks healing.

The self-healing distortion is effected through the realization of {term:intelligent-infinity} resting within. When there is no blockage, these energies pour into the being, perfecting the body moment by moment. When blockage exists, the flow is interrupted and the body manifests the result.

One of the most common sources of blockage is the feeling of unworthiness. When the entity does not believe itself worthy of the energy that is its birthright, the indigo-ray center constricts. The influx of healing energy is reduced. The remedy is circular: acknowledgment of worthiness opens the gate that unworthiness guards.

The spirit complex is the least distorted of the three aspects — a pathway or shuttle through which individual energy of will reaches upward and creative fire descends. When the mind is single-pointed and balanced, and the body comfortable, the spirit becomes a functioning communicator between the finite and the infinite.

Even a {term:wanderer} from higher densities must do this balancing work in third density before becoming a channel for healing. The incarnate limitations apply to all. The wanderer's advantage is not ability but desire — the desire to serve through this method.

Much of what entities experience as disease is the product of unprocessed catalyst. Emotional energy neither accepted nor channeled creates a bodily analog. Destructive thought patterns, left unaddressed, show themselves through the body in increasingly obvious ways.

Such conditions are correspondingly amenable to self-healing once the mechanism of the destructive influence is grasped. The healing involves not merely forgiving the other-self but forgiving the self and developing a greatly heightened respect for the self.

The body is a creature of the mind's creation, with its own polarities. The entity examines how feelings and emotions affect different portions of the body. The bodily biases must be understood, and then the opposite bias allowed full expression in understanding. Only when these are seen and accepted can the body achieve its own form of balance.

Perhaps the greatest healer is within the self. Continued meditation opens access to this inner healer. Many forms of healing available among the peoples of this world each have virtue and may be deemed appropriate. The forms are many; the principle is one: the entity heals itself.

Physical healing is not separate from spiritual growth. It is the same path. The one who does the work of balancing energy centers, accepting the self including the body, and recognizing the intelligent infinity within — this self has already begun to heal.
{term:karma} — the inertia of actions set in motion — continues until met by its antidote: {term:forgiveness}. The two concepts are inseparable.

At any point within a single life, both the self and any involved other-self may, through the process of understanding, acceptance, and forgiveness, dissolve karmic patterns. The entity that has caused harm and truly forgives the self has already begun to heal. The entity that has been harmed and truly forgives the other has released both parties from the cycle.

Forgiveness is not a formality or a spiritual performance. It is a genuine act of compassion directed inward — an acknowledgment that the pattern of action need no longer continue. When forgiveness comes, the inertia ceases instantly and completely, regardless of how many lifetimes the pattern has persisted.

Healing at its deepest level is remembering. It is the removal of the forgetting. The balancing, the healing, the slow and patient work of self-knowledge — all of it serves this one purpose: not to make the entity into something new, but to help it recall what it has always been.
